facts.statement: The genus Latirhinus was named in 2012 based on a partial skeleton found in the Campanian-age Cerro del Pueblo Formation.
facts.quote: The type species, Latirhinus uitstlani, was named in 2012 on the basis of a partial skeleton from the Campanian-age Cerro del Pueblo Formation.

facts.statement: The initial specimen found by Don Ramón López was a 6-meter-long juvenile weighing an estimated 3 tons, of which 65% was recovered.
facts.quote: The specimen was found by Don Ramón López, which was a juvenile specimen of 6 meters long, 2.2 height at the waist, and an estimated weight of 3 tons, of which 65% was recovered.

facts.statement: Latirhinus was a medium-sized hadrosaur measuring 8.7 meters long and weighing around 3.75 metric tons.
facts.quote: Latirhinus was a medium-sized hadrosaur, measuring 8.7 m long and weighing around 3.75 MT.

facts.statement: Latirhinus was likely a gregarious hadrosaur with a low back and a very broad nose.
facts.quote: Latirhinus era probablemente un hadrosáurido gregario, con una longitud aproximada a los , que poseía un lomo bajo y una nariz muy ancha.

facts.statement: The specific name uitstlani means "southern" in Náhuatl, referencing the species' occurrence in the southern part of the Cretaceous landmass Laramidia.
facts.quote: The specific name uitstlani means "southern" in the Náhuatl language of Mexico, a reference to the species' southern occurrence in the Cretaceous landmass Laramidia.

facts.statement: The time range for Latirhinus is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2012 study determined that the holotype originally defined as a saurolophine was actually a chimera, with the bones belonging to a lambeosaurine.
facts.quote: Latirhinus was originally thought to be similar to the saurolophine Gryposaurus. However, a 2012 study found its holotype, as originally defined, to be a chimera comprising both lambeosaurine and saurolophine remains; the holotype bones would've belonged to a lambeosaurine.

facts.statement: There are still disagreements among researchers regarding the specific position of Latirhinus within the Lambeosaurinae.
facts.quote: While this position has been accepted by other researchers, there are still disagreements over where Latirhinus falls within Lambeosaurinae.

facts.statement: Cladograms show conflicting positions for Latirhinus, with some placing it as a basal lambeosaurine and others as a derived member of Lambeosaurini.
facts.quote: El primer cladograma muestra a Latirhinus como un lambeosaurino basal, mientras que el segundo muestra una posición alternativa como miembro derivado de Lambeosaurini.

facts.statement: Latirhinus lived contemporaneously with Velafrons coahuilensis, Kritosaurus navajovius, Coahuilaceratops magnacuerna, Paraxenisaurus normalensis, and the marine turtle Mexichelys in the Cerro del Pueblo Formation.
facts.quote: Latirhinus fue contemporáneo en la Formación Cerro del Pueblo de los hadrosáuridos Velafrons coahuilensis y Kritosaurus navajovius del ceratopsio Coahuilaceratops magnacuerna, el ornitomimosaurio Paraxenisaurus normalensis así como un género extinto de tortuga marina Mexichelys.
